checkpoints.naturalness: Playful gala introductions establish readable occupational voices; uniformly punchy jokes feel like a cast roll call.
checkpoints.reasoning: No murder evidence yet. Hints of financial and provenance disputes supply possibilities, but no individual deserves a meaningful lead.

checkpoints.naturalness: Documents create a credible bureaucracy and several distinct conflicts, though sixteen fragments are demanding to absorb. The historical poison and engraved toast glass strongly foreshadow a method.
checkpoints.reasoning: Artie faces forced resignation, Barb can hide camera access, Brie controls private service. Poison bottle can connect curatorial/conservation access with hospitality; no murder or actual tampering evidence yet.

checkpoints.naturalness: Abrupt official notice makes the death feel procedural, but the conditional nature of the gift is useful and clear.
checkpoints.reasoning: Death follows the private toast, so access to its drink and glass rises in importance. Brie has most direct role. The unsigned proposals may motivate staff but do not demonstrate an irreversible threat.

checkpoints.naturalness: Personal admissions add satisfying human stakes, especially payroll, caregiving and Reed wanting credit. Almost everyone follows the same confession-plus-vulnerability rhythm, which becomes noticeable across twenty-two speeches.
checkpoints.reasoning: Hugh faces public fraud exposure, Artie loses position, and Barb enabled a concealed room. Brie has access but the unpaid addition seems weaker than careers and fraud. Most motives remain reversible professional disputes; actual timing and poison access must discriminate.

checkpoints.naturalness: Concrete clock times and isolated contamination turn the mystery into an actionable puzzle. The hidden broken seal is a strong clue without naming a suspect.
checkpoints.reasoning: Cyanide likely transferred from historical bottle into the individual glass while unattended between 6:32 and 7:04, or by service after collection. The shared punch is cleared. Staff-accessible preparation cupboard makes institutional access relevant; Brie and Barb remain strongest access candidates, but bottle knowledge could distinguish a curator, conservator or commissioned painter.

checkpoints.naturalness: The exchanges deepen relationships and embarrassment, but the orderly groups all volunteering incriminating modifications feel engineered. Al sitting beside the waiting glass and Brie bringing flavoring are especially tangible.
checkpoints.reasoning: Hugh and Dr. Art E. Fact knew original contents contradicted inert labeling; Claire and Reed had access to full papers. Chip handled closure. Al, Tess, Dada, Barb and Brie explicitly approached the waiting glass. Al combines preview and private-glass access; Brie directly introduced drink flavoring. Need witness timing and what each could know rather than trusting any confession.

checkpoints.naturalness: Evidence is detailed and mostly helpful, but this is a large administrative bundle with many settled side issues. References to nonsuspect photographers, handlers and podcast producers distract. Dates in late October conflict with current calendar but can simply be fictional chronology.
checkpoints.reasoning: The physical poison bottle, exposed glass, real ingestion and disabled recording are supported. Staff knew the original-contents conflict and had keys. Brie supplied clean flavoring but could separately poison glass; Barb had room and key access. Monet has payroll misconduct plus service-ticket movement, though no direct glass contact yet. Reduced settlements and withdrawn refund demands weaken several motives without eliminating opportunity. Similar band stock has no unique edge match, so cannot alone identify handler.

checkpoints.naturalness: Al suddenly makes a very specific material claim against a plainly contrary retained surface sample. That is a clear solve signal. Emotional closing remarks work well individually, though repeated self-confession and addresses to colleagues create a shared cadence.
checkpoints.reasoning: Al asserts the red-faced silver-backed scrap came from his sculpture and that he personally cut such leaf, while retained sample identifies bronze powder and gold leaf, not red foil-backed paper. His earlier preview attendance and sitting by the unattended glass offer the required transfer opportunity, with reduced payment and caregiving pressure a motive. Other suspicious acts have independent explanations; his false account directly contests evidence at the poisoned glass.

final_accusation.reasoning: He supplies the uniquely false account of the material in the poisoned glass: sculpture surface sample is bronze powder and gold transfer leaf, whereas glass scrap resembles red foil-backed bottle closure paper. He attended the bottle preview and later sat beside the unwrapped unattended glass. His final settlement was reduced while someone at home depended on him.

final_feedback.logic: The final material contradiction yields a clear leading accusation. It is stronger as a consciousness-of-guilt inference than a forensic identity proof, since the paper has no unique torn edge and an innocent suspect could wrongly attribute a scrap. Bottle access, glass access and financial stakes support the inference.
final_feedback.alternative_theories: Chip supplied the actual band and had poison access; Barb disabled the camera and checked the empty room; Brie added something directly to the glass. Those remain mechanically possible unless one privileges the distinctive false claim. Al may have seen the short inert caption; his exact knowledge of active poison is less explicit than that of collection staff.
final_feedback.storytelling: Rich professional anxieties and personal vulnerabilities make the suspects human, especially payroll, caregiving, scholarship and family approval. Side-account resolutions multiply administrative reading and sometimes dilute tension. Twenty-two evenly paced admissions are demanding; sharper variation in answer length and resistance would strengthen natural dialogue.

post_vote_feedback.outcome: Correctly accused Al Baster before opening the endings.
post_vote_feedback.logic: Confession confirms the material contradiction and both opportunities. It carefully acknowledges that scrap similarity was not a unique match. The confession adds certainty of bottle opening and intentional poisoning beyond the pre-vote inferential case.
post_vote_feedback.storytelling: Many endings provide credible costs and relationship changes: Monet faces the board, Barb returns her badge, Claire gives Reed access, Penny accepts losing control, and Brie protects staff. Al tying caregiving to a justification rejected by the dependent is emotionally effective. Every character explains their evidence and then articulates a healthier choice, so the collective closure has a noticeable uniform redemption pattern.
post_vote_feedback.remaining_issue: Al learning the contents were active is less explicit in pre-vote evidence than his physical access. The final specific false material claim makes him conspicuous only at stage 8.

protocol_deviation: None. Read checkpoints 1 through 8 in order, saving all named ratings and checking successful Python exit before each next read. Saved final accusation and feedback before opening post-vote endings. No rescoring afterward; no other source files read.
